brief.inclusion: Israeli-American physician, controlling Las Vegas Sands shareholder, newspaper publisher, sports-franchise owner, philanthropist and one of the largest disclosed Republican donors in the United States.

summary: Miriam Adelson trained as an Israeli physician and built addiction-treatment clinics before joining her husband Sheldon Adelson in philanthropy, media ownership and Republican politics. After his death in 2021, she became the central public figure in a family network that controls most voting power at Las Vegas Sands, publishes Israel Hayom and owns a majority interest in the Dallas Mavericks. Her political influence rests on exceptionally large disclosed federal contributions, a durable alliance with Donald Trump and sustained advocacy for Israel, while her medical and charitable institutions remain distinct from her campaign spending.

chapters.title: An Israeli medical formation came first
chapters.dek: Adelson's public life began in medicine decades before casino ownership made her a political financier.
chapters.body:
Miriam Farbstein was born in Tel Aviv on October 10, 1945, before the establishment of the State of Israel, and grew up in Haifa. Her parents had left Poland before the Holocaust. That family history and Israel's early statehood became lasting elements of her public identity, but they do not by themselves explain the political choices she later made. [[adelson-foundation-bio, rockefeller-bio]]

She studied microbiology and genetics at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and earned a medical degree, magna cum laude, at Tel Aviv University. She trained in internal and emergency medicine and became a head physician at Rokach Hospital in Tel Aviv. [[adelson-foundation-bio, rockefeller-bio]]

The record matters because “casino billionaire” describes the wealth she later controlled, not the professional identity she first built. Her medical credentials and addiction research were substantive careers rather than honorary affiliations acquired after wealth. [[rockefeller-bio, adelson-clinic]]

chapters.title: Addiction treatment became her independent institution
chapters.dek: Clinics in Tel Aviv and Las Vegas linked research, medication and long-term care.
chapters.body:
Beginning in 1986, Adelson concentrated on drug dependence and the biological effects of addiction. She helped establish a Tel Aviv clinic in 1993 that was affiliated with a hospital, reinforcing the argument that addiction should be treated as disease rather than only crime or moral failure. [[adelson-foundation-bio, adelson-clinic]]

She married casino entrepreneur Sheldon Adelson in 1991. After dividing time between Israel and the United States, the family opened a Las Vegas clinic in 2000. The program used medication-assisted treatment and served adults and adolescents, with family philanthropy supporting operations and research. [[adelson-foundation-bio, adelson-clinic]]

The clinics also provided the foundation for later public honors. They were philanthropic institutions, but their medical purpose and professional management should be assessed separately from the couple's campaign contributions or casino interests. [[adelson-clinic, white-house-medal-2018]]

chapters.title: Wealth scaled a transnational philanthropic network
chapters.dek: The Adelsons joined medical giving to Jewish education, Holocaust memory and support for Israel.
chapters.body:
As Las Vegas Sands expanded in the United States and Asia, Miriam and Sheldon Adelson built a family foundation able to make large grants. Its priorities included medical research, Jewish schools, Holocaust memorial organizations, Birthright Israel and groups connecting American Jewish life with Israel. [[adelson-foundation-bio, adelson-foundation-vision, white-house-medal-2018]]

Adelson's giving combined universal medical claims with an explicit national and religious commitment. She described Jewish continuity and defense of Israel as obligations rather than neutral charitable categories. Those first-person positions provide better evidence of her worldview than attempts to infer politics from identity alone. [[adelson-foundation-vision, israel-hayom-israel-real]]

The foundation's grants and her personal political contributions operate under different legal regimes. A full account connects them where they share institutions or stated goals, while refusing to add charitable spending to campaign-finance totals. [[adelson-foundation-bio, fec-adelson]]

chapters.title: The family became a political institution of its own
chapters.dek: Very large checks gave the Adelsons repeated leverage in Republican primaries, general elections and policy debates.
chapters.body:
The Adelsons became leading Republican financiers during the Obama era, supporting candidates, party committees and outside groups. Their giving favored hawkish U.S. policy toward Iran, strong support for Israel and conservative domestic politics. The scale allowed candidates to seek their support as a strategic event, but a contribution is evidence of access and preference—not proof that a later policy was purchased. [[time-sheldon-2021, fec-adelson]]

They initially supported other Republicans in 2016 before backing Donald Trump. In 2020 they supplied $90 million to Preserve America, a super PAC supporting his reelection. Super PAC gifts can be unlimited because the committee must remain legally independent of the campaign, even when donor and candidate goals align. [[factcheck-preserve-2024, reuters-adelson-trump-2024]]

After Sheldon's death, Miriam demonstrated that the operation was not solely her husband's. In 2024 she became Preserve America's principal funder, including $95 million reported during the third quarter, and also gave to a Kemp-aligned group organizing turnout in Georgia. [[axios-donors-2024, ap-kemp-2024, fec-adelson]]

chapters.title: Trump turned donor access into visible policy alliance
chapters.dek: Jerusalem, the Golan Heights and the Medal of Freedom made the relationship unusually public.
chapters.body:
The Adelsons sought policies that recognized Jerusalem as Israel's capital, confronted Iran and strengthened the U.S.–Israel alliance. Trump moved the U.S. embassy to Jerusalem in 2018, and Miriam Adelson celebrated the decision in her own newspaper as beneficial to both countries. [[israel-hayom-jerusalem-2018, israel-hayom-thanks-2021]]

In November 2018 Trump awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom, citing addiction medicine, philanthropy and support for Jewish organizations. The honor recognized real medical and charitable work, while its award by a president whose party the Adelsons had heavily financed inevitably raised patronage questions. The record supports both facts without requiring one to cancel the other. [[white-house-medal-2018, medal-ceremony-2018, time-sheldon-2021]]

Trump later spoke openly about the couple's frequent White House visits and their advocacy on Israel policy. His account is evidence of access and influence, not a complete causal record for decisions also supported by evangelical voters, Republican officials and Israeli governments. [[reuters-israel-influence-2025, israel-hayom-thanks-2021]]

chapters.title: Sheldon Adelson's death did not dissolve the network
chapters.dek: Miriam became the central public steward of family capital, philanthropy, media and political giving.
chapters.body:
Sheldon Adelson died on January 11, 2021. Obituaries emphasized his role as Las Vegas Sands founder and Republican kingmaker, but the couple had long acted together in philanthropy and politics. Miriam's own medicine, writing and advocacy supplied an independent public identity. [[time-sheldon-2021, adelson-foundation-bio]]

Control passed through shares, trusts and family entities rather than a simple inheritance of one job title. Las Vegas Sands employed Adelson as co-founder and special adviser while professional executives operated the company. SEC filings identify a reporting group in which she and family trusts collectively held majority voting power. [[lvs-proxy-2025, lvs-13d-2025]]

She also remained publisher of Israel Hayom and continued first-person political commentary. Ownership can shape an outlet's institutional direction, but individual articles still have authors and editors; the profile attributes Adelson's own columns to her and does not treat every news story as her statement. [[israel-hayom-about, israel-hayom-israel-real]]

chapters.title: Corporate control expanded into American sports
chapters.dek: The Mavericks purchase made the family a Texas civic and business power as well as a casino shareholder.
chapters.body:
Las Vegas Sands's 2025 proxy reported that Adelson, trusts and associated family entities collectively controlled 54.7% of the company's outstanding stock. Adelson herself was listed with 48.6% beneficial ownership, but SEC footnotes distinguish direct interests, options, trusts and group attribution. Those categories should not be collapsed into a personal cash figure. [[lvs-proxy-2025, lvs-13d-2025]]

In December 2023 the NBA approved the Adelson-Dumont families' acquisition of the Dallas Mavericks' controlling interest from Mark Cuban at a valuation around $3.5 billion. Son-in-law Patrick Dumont became the team's governor, while Cuban retained a minority stake. [[nba-mavericks-sale, nba-sale-analysis]]

The transaction connected a global resort operator with a major Texas institution. It increased the family's civic reach and commercial stake in the state, but team ownership is a business relationship distinct from Adelson's personal federal donations and from any future Texas debate about casinos. [[nba-mavericks-sale, nba-sale-analysis, fec-adelson]]

chapters.title: A newspaper gives her influence beyond checks
chapters.dek: Israel Hayom joins capital, editorial voice and transnational political advocacy in a single institution.
chapters.body:
Israel Hayom identifies Miriam Adelson as its publisher. The free newspaper has been a major presence in Israeli media, and the Adelson family's ownership made it part of debates over press power and political alignment. Ownership is influence over an institution, but it is not proof that the publisher dictates each report. [[israel-hayom-about]]

Adelson also writes under her own name. Her columns praised Trump's Jerusalem decision, endorsed him in 2024 and described Jewish sovereignty as a historical achievement requiring gratitude and defense. These texts make her substantive positions explicit rather than inferred from donations alone. [[israel-hayom-jerusalem-2018, israel-hayom-trump-2024, israel-hayom-israel-real]]

The combination is unusual: a U.S. megadonor also publishes a leading newspaper in another democracy. That gives her parallel channels—campaign finance in the United States and agenda-setting speech in Israel—while the legal and editorial systems remain separate. [[israel-hayom-about, fec-adelson]]

chapters.title: By 2026, her donor power was independent and durable
chapters.dek: Midterm giving showed that Adelson financed the party as well as one presidential candidate.
chapters.body:
Adelson's 2024 support helped give Trump an outside spending operation capable of sustained advertising in the final months. She publicly endorsed him in Israel Hayom, aligning her money with a clear policy and leadership argument rather than presenting the contributions as ideologically neutral. [[axios-donors-2024, israel-hayom-trump-2024]]

In April 2026 she gave $40 million to super PACs aligned with Republican Senate and House leaders, including $30 million to the Senate group. The contributions broadened her role beyond presidential politics and placed her among the central financiers of the party's attempt to retain Congress. [[bloomberg-midterms-2026, fec-adelson]]

As of October 22, 2026, Adelson's influence rests on several assets that should be measured separately: disclosed campaign money, majority-family corporate control, ownership of media and sports institutions, philanthropy, and direct relationships with political leaders. The FEC tab can count the first category; the rest require filings, institutional records and attributed reporting rather than a single dollar total. [[lvs-proxy-2025, nba-mavericks-sale, israel-hayom-about, bloomberg-midterms-2026]]
